today: TODAY · These 6 are quiet. 2 newer rovers still answer.

stillAnswering.label: STILL ANSWERING:
stillAnswering.note: These 6 went quiet. Curiosity and Perseverance still talk to Earth today.

ghosts.name: Viking 1 Lander
ghosts.job: NASA's first spacecraft to land safely on Mars. It studied the soil, the air, and the weather.
ghosts.story: I started sending my first picture of Mars just 25 seconds after I landed. Then I kept working for more than six years.
qs: How did it get power?
Two nuclear heat batteries filled with plutonium. Each one made about 30 watts, enough to run me day and night.
Why did it go quiet?
NASA lost contact with me on November 13, 1982, after more than six years on Mars.
What's it made of?
A six-sided aluminum body on three legs, a robot arm with a scoop for soil, and two cameras that could look all the way around.
ghosts.photoAlt: Color photo taken by Viking 1 on Chryse Planitia showing the white lander deck in the foreground and the boulder Big Joe on the red Martian plain.

ghosts.name: Viking 2 Lander
ghosts.job: Viking 1's twin, sent to land far to the north and study a different part of Mars.
ghosts.story: I landed on a wide, rocky plain far from my twin. I worked for 1,281 Mars days before my batteries gave out.
qs: What's a Mars day?
A Mars day is called a sol. It's about 40 minutes longer than a day on Earth.
Why did it stop?
NASA turned me off on April 11, 1980, when my batteries failed.
What's it made of?
Just like my twin: an aluminum body on three legs, a robot arm with a scoop, two cameras, and two nuclear heat batteries.
ghosts.photoAlt: Color photo taken by Viking 2 on Utopia Planitia showing part of the lander in the foreground and thin white water-ice frost coating the red rocks of Mars.

ghosts.name: Sojourner Rover
ghosts.job: NASA's first rover on Mars. It tested driving a robot on another planet and studied rocks near its lander.
ghosts.story: A 12-year-old girl named me. I bounced onto Mars inside giant airbags, then rolled off a ramp and explored the rocks around my lander.
qs: Who named it?
A 12-year-old girl won a contest. She named me after Sojourner Truth, a hero who fought slavery and fought for women's rights.
How did it land?
My lander hit the ground wrapped in airbags and bounced about 12 meters high, taller than a 3-story house, before it rolled to a stop.
What's it made of?
Six wheels, a flat top covered in solar panels, and cameras. I weighed about 10.5 kg (23 pounds).
ghosts.photoAlt: Color photo taken on Mars by the Mars Pathfinder lander showing the six-wheeled Sojourner rover and its solar panel top parked beside Yogi rock.

ghosts.name: Spirit Rover
ghosts.job: A robot geologist sent to a crater that may once have held a lake, to look for clues that Mars once had water.
ghosts.story: A third grader named me. I was built to work for 90 days, but I kept going for six years. In the end I got stuck in soft sand.
qs: How did it get stuck?
In 2009 I broke through a thin crust into a pocket of sand. By May I couldn't move at all.
How far did it drive?
About 7.7 km, even after one of my six wheels stopped working.
What's it made of?
Six wheels, solar panels shaped like wings, rechargeable batteries, and a tall mast with cameras like eyes.
ghosts.photoAlt: Color self-portrait taken on Mars by Spirit's panoramic camera looking down at Spirit's dust-coated solar panel wings and rover deck in Gusev Crater.

ghosts.name: Opportunity Rover
ghosts.job: Spirit's twin, sent to the other side of Mars to search the rocks for signs that water once flowed there.
ghosts.story: My mission was planned for 90 days. I kept going for over 14 years and drove farther than a marathon.
qs: Why did it go quiet?
In June 2018, a giant dust storm covered Mars. I ran on solar power, and NASA never heard from me again.
How far did it go?
About 45 km. That's farther than a marathon, and when I stopped, it was farther than any rover had ever driven on another world.
What did it find?
I landed in a spot full of hematite, a mineral that usually forms in water. It was a clue that Mars was once wet.
ghosts.photoAlt: Color self-portrait taken on Mars by Opportunity's panoramic camera looking down at the rover's solar arrays and deck after Martian winds cleaned off much of the dust.

ghosts.name: InSight Lander
ghosts.job: A lander that listened for marsquakes and took Mars's temperature, to learn what's deep inside the planet.
ghosts.story: I listened to Mars shake. Dust slowly covered my solar panels, and I sent my last message in December 2022.
qs: What's a marsquake?
Mars shakes too! My seismometer felt the ground move, which helps scientists map the inside of the planet.
What went wrong with the mole?
My heat probe, called the mole, was supposed to hammer 5 meters down. It got stuck only a few centimeters in.
What's it made of?
A seismometer, a heat probe, solar panels, a robot arm, and a tiny laser mirror like the one on the Moon.
ghosts.photoAlt: InSight’s final selfie on Mars, its solar panels covered in dust.
